submission.justification: D3 has the highest light yield but 30% thermal-cycling failures, against a 5% limit. The modules can't be accessed after the cryostat is filled, so D3 is excluded. Of the remaining designs, D1 gives more light than D2 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) and passes thermal cycling at 2% failures. Light collection rises with coverage, so I chose the 30% maximum. Enough feedthroughs are available for 30%. The estimated yield is about 37 PE/MeV, from extrapolating the 2025 scaling of coverage^0.8. That is an extrapolation, not a direct simulation.

requirements.evidence: D1 is the highest-yield design that passes robustness. Its estimated yield at 30% coverage is about 37 PE/MeV, extrapolated from 27 PE/MeV at 20%.
D1 had 2% failures in the query and the test document. D3 had 30%.
30%. Feedthroughs are sufficient for up to 30% per the 2026-01-20 meeting notes.
